answer: To curb Sybil attacks, an agent network can require bonded collateral staking. Participants lock assets into an escrow lagoon and sign task commitments using a cryptographic quill. An audit lantern tracks interactions, slashing deposits whenever duplicate personas or invalid states appear. This forces adversaries to incur the verifiable cost of locked capital per identity. However, wealthy attackers can absorb these stake expenses, while high deposit thresholds exclude capital-poor agents.
